decisions.rationale: Escalated to the captain (project-row delivery decision): the confirmed coverage matrix treats calendar Project rows as overlay metadata only, with no authored project brief, scaffold or tests. Authoring a required project artifact for this row expands that scope. Hold until the decision returns; apply the other accepted decisions now.

Labs use the learner-local PostgreSQL installation that the syllabus already requires (no container), through pinned pgJDBC. One Maven test command creates an isolated database or schema from documented environment-based connection settings, runs the tests and cleans up, on macOS, Linux and Windows. H2 stays only where the author and SME can show the targeted behaviour transfers, and never for psql or PostgreSQL-only claims. Whether F23 gets a required project artifact follows the escalated project decision.

Revise representative coverage so the coding format elicits at least one central JDBC outcome: map JDBC review o1 (connect, prepare, execute, read, close) to coding. Keep the frozen MCQ and coding formats, the 45-minute block and the pass mark. Any F23 project-objective mapping follows the escalated project decision.

Remove pagination from the Filtering and sorting objectives; o3 becomes predicting deterministic ordering with explicit sort keys. Map the blueprint to a filtering or sorting objective named by the frozen syllabus.
Same resolution as sql-intake-edu-002: the JDBC work runs against learner-local PostgreSQL through pinned pgJDBC with one Maven command and environment-based connection settings, and no container.

The queries lab runs against learner-local PostgreSQL. The seed-script path runs through real psql (\copy) from the single Maven entry command, so o3 is genuinely validated. Do not claim H2 coverage of psql.

Add an authoritative first-party normalization source (for example the sampled Microsoft Learn explanation, with receipt) mapped to o1/o2, or keep the source-gap record open. Preserve the PostgreSQL key and constraint sources.
